dedupe_keys.name: report itu r bt 2299 4 broadcasting for public warning disaster mitigation and relief september 2025

description: This ITU-R report compiles evidence that terrestrial radio and television broadcasting is critically important for informing the public in emergencies such as storms, floods, earthquakes, tsunamis, solar storms and technological disasters. It is organised in eleven sections: background and advantages of terrestrial broadcasting, broadcasters' experience gathering public safety information, operational methods that keep services on air, use of existing infrastructure for emergency communication, new techniques and systems, collaboration between organisations, public service efforts, international broadcasting for disaster relief, previous ITU-R documents, case studies with links to video documentaries, and conclusions. Annexes give broadcaster experience from countries and organisations, for example the Australian Broadcasting Corporation, and the text describes NHK's emergency transmission vehicles introduced after the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake. The 2025 edition is the fourth revision, with earlier versions in 2015 and 2017. Producer: ITU-R, Geneva, September 2025, 17 pages. Coverage: global. Access: free PDF; the foreword, introduction, table of contents and the start of the sections were read. Licence and cost: free to download; all rights reserved. Caveats: it is a narrative compilation with no measured performance data. Simulation uses: the operating methods and case studies inform emergency-response and continuity scenarios for broadcast networks. Related records: the ITU Asia Media Summit early warning slides (data-itu-broadcasting-national-early-warning-resilience-strategy-ams-2025) and the US nationwide alert test of 2023 (case_study-us-nationwide-alert-test-2023).
